findings.text: Extended identification and feature leaf uses four register words. The first word groups stepping, base model, base family, base type and extended model and family with reserved spacing. The second word groups brand identification with package type. The other two words are one-bit capability signals for virtualization, memory management, power, profiling and media behavior, including topoext and svm on one side and syscall, lm, nx and pae on the other, with reserved bits interspersed.

Three consecutive leaves each carry four full-width character words that together encode a readable processor name. Each word holds one four-byte slice of the name, so each leaf contributes sixteen bytes. Field names distinguish successive slices across the three leaves.

Brand slices form a continuous sequence from early to late bytes across the three leaves in numeric leaf order, starting with the lowest-numbered slice in the lowest leaf and ending with the highest-numbered slice in the highest leaf. No control, length or encoding field is shown alongside the character data.

First-level cache and translation leaf uses four words. The first two words report translation entry counts and associativity, separated by instruction versus data use and by large versus small page size. The remaining two words report data-cache then instruction-cache geometry as line size, lines per tag, associativity and total size.

Second-level translation plus second- and third-level cache leaf uses four words. The first two words report instruction and data translation counts and associativity for large and small pages with narrower associativity fields than the first-level leaf. The third word reports second-level line size, lines per tag, associativity and total size, while the fourth word reports third-level line size, lines per tag, associativity and a size range with reserved space.

Reliability and power-thermal leaf reserves the first word, reports recoverability and containment capabilities in the second word, carries a single power sampling ratio scalar in the third word, and packs thermal sensing plus frequency, voltage, boost and power-reporting signals in the fourth word, including rapl_interface, digital_temp and constant_tsc with substantial reserved space.

Address-size and extended-capability leaf uses four words. The first word gives maximum physical, virtual and nested-guest physical widths. The second word is a large one-bit capability set for cache maintenance, speculation controls, branch barriers and performance or inventory features, including amd_ssbd, clzero, stibp and ibpb among many others. The third word reports thread count and identifier sizing, while the fourth word reports invalidate and register-read limits.

Virtual-machine control leaf reports a revision number in the first word, a full-width address-space identifier count in the second word, a page-logging signal in the third word, and a broad virtualization capability set in the fourth word covering nested paging, interrupt and timer virtualization, pause filtering and related controls, including nested_pt, avic and nrip_save with reserved gaps.

Large-page translation leaf reports entry counts and associativity for one-gigabyte pages, split by first-level versus second-level and instruction versus data use across the first two words. The remaining two words are fully reserved.

Execution-width hint leaf uses only the low bits of the first word to signal internal floating and vector datapath widths and a move-form preference, including fp_128, fp_256 and movu_preferred. All other bits in that word and all remaining words are reserved.

Sampling-feature leaf concentrates capability signals in the first word for fetch and execution sampling, counter behavior, branch target reporting and filtering extensions, including ibs_l3_miss_filter, ibs_branch_target and ibs_op_sampling. All other words are fully reserved.

Lightweight profiling leaf mirrors operating-system and hardware availability views in the outer words, with matching event, mode and overflow signals including os_lwp_avail, hw_lwp_avail and threshold-interrupt behavior. The inner words encode control-block and event-record sizing plus latency, version, buffering and filtering capabilities, including lwp_version.

Deterministic cache leaf describes one cache level per subleaf across four words. The first word identifies cache type, level, self-initialization, full associativity and sharing count. The second word gives line size, partitions and associativity in zero-based form. The third word gives the set count in zero-based form, and the fourth word records inclusivity and remote-invalidate guarantees.
First valid subleaf index for the deterministic cache leaf is 0.
Last valid subleaf index for the deterministic cache leaf is 31, so 32 indices are defined.

Extended topology leaf carries a full-width extended APIC identifier in the first word, per-core identity and thread count in the second word, and node identity plus nodes-per-package in the third word. The final word is fully reserved.

Confidential-memory leaf packs encryption and virtualization security capabilities in the first word, including vm_permission_levels, sme and sev among many single-bit signals. The second word gives the encryption-bit position, physical-address reduction and permission-level count. The third word gives the maximum simultaneous encrypted guests, and the fourth word gives the minimum identifier floor for a selected guest mode.
Quality-of-service base leaf reserves three words and uses the second word for allocation and monitoring support signals, including abmc, l3rr and mba with large reserved space.

Two companion leaves report enforcement sizing for standard and slow-memory bandwidth allocation. Each uses the first word for a limit length and the last word for a zero-based maximum class-of-service number, with middle words reserved.

Monitoring-configuration leaf reports the available bandwidth-event count in the second word and a set of trackable traffic classes in the third word covering local and remote reads, non-temporal writes, slow-memory reads and dirty-victim traffic. All other words are reserved.

Each leaf structure maps its four declaration groups to the four result registers in order, with every group widths summing to one full word. Unnamed fields denote reserved space that software must not interpret, and fully reserved words carry no defined signals.
